summary:
​Silent Witnesses on the Moon (Apollo 11–17)

 
NASA's Apollo missions, conducted between 1969 and 1972, were a colossal feat of engineering, marking the first human landings outside of Earth. In the six successful manned missions (Apollo 11, 12, 14, 15, 16, and 17) that landed on the Moon, minimizing the launch weight was a vital necessity for the astronauts' safe return to Earth. The Lunar Module's ascent stage, which was to rendezvous with the Command Module waiting in orbit, had a limited fuel capacity, only capable of carrying the crew, flight records, and collected lunar rocks. Naturally, to ensure the rocket could return to Earth, they needed to minimize its weight. Therefore, they had to leave behind heavy equipment and vehicles once their work was done on the Moon. Today, over 180,000 kilograms of man-made material silently rests on the lunar surface.
